- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often overestimates — apply 3–5% downward bias for 10-day horizon.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often underestimates — add 3–5% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8% to align with historical volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ in last 5 days), reduce forecast smoothing weight by 20% to reflect uncertainty.
